\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فساد} (fasād)}{فساد (fasād)}]{\ur{فساد} (fasād) — a riot; strife}

\label{lesson:UR-C304-fasad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for information, then the Urdu for the reality.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فساد}}
\textbf{\ur{فساد}} — \emph{fasād} — \textquotedblleft{}a riot; strife\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{فساد} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahr meṅ fasād huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a riot in the city.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فساد}} (\emph{fasād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{fasād}, \textquotedblleft{}corruption, disorder\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu it is most often violence between groups.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahr meṅ fasād huā.} — There was a riot in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for information, then the Urdu for the reality, then say \emph{fasād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{فساد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A riot; strife\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہنگامہ} (hangāmā)}{ہنگامہ (hangāmā)}]{\ur{ہنگامہ} (hangāmā) — an uproar; a commotion}

\label{lesson:UR-C304-hangama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the reality, then the Urdu for a riot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہنگامہ}}
\textbf{\ur{ہنگامہ}} — \emph{hangāmā} — \textquotedblleft{}an uproar; a commotion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بازار} \ur{میں} \ur{ہنگامہ} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāzār meṅ hangāmā huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was an uproar in the market.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہنگامہ}} (\emph{hangāmā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hangāma}, \textquotedblleft{}a crowd, a tumult\textquotedblright{}. It is noise and disorder, which need not turn violent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھوٹنا} (phūṭnā)}{پھوٹنا (phūṭnā)}]{\ur{پھوٹنا} (phūṭnā) — to burst; to break out}

\label{lesson:UR-C304-phutna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a riot, then the Urdu for an uproar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھوٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھوٹنا}} — \emph{phūṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to burst; to break out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{اچانک} \ur{فساد} \ur{پھوٹ} \ur{پڑا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt ko achānak fasād phūṭ paṛā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Suddenly, in the night, a riot broke out.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بوتل} \ur{پھوٹی}, \emph{voh botal phūṭī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھوٹنا}} (\emph{phūṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{phūṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to split, to burst\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 13845). Trouble \textbf{\ur{پھوٹ} \ur{پڑا}} when it broke out all at once.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لاٹھی} (lāṭhī)}{لاٹھی (lāṭhī)}]{\ur{لاٹھی} (lāṭhī) — a stick; a police baton}

\label{lesson:UR-C304-lathi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an uproar, then the Urdu for to break out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لاٹھی}}
\textbf{\ur{لاٹھی}} — \emph{lāṭhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a stick; a police baton\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لاٹھی}} (\emph{lāṭhī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lāṭhī}, \textquotedblleft{}a staff, a club\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10991). It is the long bamboo stick of the police.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کرفیو} (karfyū)}{کرفیو (karfyū)}]{\ur{کرفیو} (karfyū) — a curfew}

\label{lesson:UR-C304-karfyu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to break out, then the Urdu for a police baton.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کرفیو}}
\textbf{\ur{کرفیو}} — \emph{karfyū} — \textquotedblleft{}a curfew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شام} \ur{سے} \ur{صبح} \ur{تک} \ur{کرفیو} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shām se subah tak karfyū thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a curfew from evening until morning.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
is borrowed from English \emph{curfew}. During a \textbf{\ur{کرفیو}} nobody may go out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
